reasoning_summary: Steps 0001-0009 are setup and a correct (if slightly informally stated) unwinding of lim f/g = infinity: for every M > 0 there is n_0 with f(n)/g(n) > M for all n >= n_0. Step 0010 multiplies through by g(n) to get f(n) > M*g(n); this tacitly assumes g(n) > 0 for large n, which is a standard but unstated hypothesis, so I did not stop there. Step 0011 is the first step that is certainly wrong: from f(n) > M*g(n) the author picks a constant c_1 satisfying 0 <= M <= c_1 and asserts 0 <= c_1*g(n) <= f(n). The inequality runs the wrong way. With g(n) > 0 and c_1 >= M we get c_1*g(n) >= M*g(n), so knowing f(n) > M*g(n) gives no lower bound of f(n) by c_1*g(n). The correct choice is c_1 <= M (e.g. fix M = 1 and take c_1 = 1), which yields c_1*g(n) <= M*g(n) < f(n). As written the Omega bound does not follow from the displayed inequality. Separately, the submission is not a completed proof at all: steps 0015-0020 explicitly ask how to prove f(n) != O(g(n)) and only sketch an unverified reductio, so the second half of the claimed statement is never established even if 0011 were repaired.
